01.steps:
1) Have the MTU on both VPN endpoinds set to default.
2) Have the checkbox Enable Fragmented Packets Handling on the VPN>Advanced page turned off.
3) Send 2000 byte packets through the VPN tunnel.
4) Turn on the checkbox Enable Fragmented Packets Handling.
5) Send 2000 byte packets through the VPN tunnel.
01.initial: Ensure that jumbo frames are enabled on the source PC and the ingress firewall interface, otherwise the PC interface driver will drop any packets with MTU larger than the configured value!
01.title: Enable Fragmented Packets checkbox is turned off -> on
01.result: The PC generates ICMP message Packet needs to be fragmented but DF set. Pings are returned. The firewall shows the log message ?Received fragmented packet or fragmentation needed. After steps 4 and 5 the pings are returned.

10.steps:
Note: One thing to note is that PMTU is per interface. That means the decision to fragment the packet or not depends on the PMTU size of eventual egress interface(i.e. if the packet came through X0, but eventually destined for X1, the additional processing such as ICMP message or dropping packet occurs if the resulting (VPN)packet size is bigger than X1’s PMTU, not X0).

1. Go to VPN-->Advanced GUI page on one of the FW

2. Enable "Enable Fragmented Packet Handling" and Enable "Ignore DF bit"

3. Note down the MTU size on the egress interface. If X1 is WAN for VPN then change the MTU to 1200 from 1500.

4. Send packets larger than MTU with DF bit ON from the sender.

To send packets larger than MTU and DF bit ON, we can use ping utility in windows:

Ping some IP address on other side of the VPN using following command:

ping x.x.x.x -f -l 1300

where, -l size send buffer size, and -f set Don't fragment flag in packets (IPv4 only)
10.initial: Two FWs with test build and VPN connection
10.title: When Enable Fragmentation is ON (Ignore DF bit is ON in FW) and DF bit on from sender
10.result:
FW accept & handle ingress ICMP PMTU messages and since ignore DF bit on FW is on, the packets should be fragmented and go through the VPN tunnel
Packet capture shows the fragmented packets
All pings should be successful via the VPN tunnel

3. Note MTU size on the egress interface such as X1 WAN and change it to 1200 from 1500

To send packets larger than MTU  and DF bit OFF, we can use ping utility in windows:

Ping some IP address on other side of the VPN using following command:

ping x.x.x.x -l 1400

where, -l size send buffer size, -f set don't fragment flag in packet (IPV4 only). remove this option for off DF bit for sender

2. Enable "Enable Fragmented Packet Handling" but disable "Ignore DF bit

4. Send Packets smaller than MTU which is configured on the FW

Ping an IP address on other side of the VPN by using following command 

ping x.x.x.x -l 400 or ping x.x.x.x -l 400 -f
